findings.description: Reusing one statistics dictionary makes nested and overlapping invocations overwrite each other's statistics. The async wrapper introduces the same loss of per-call isolation.
findings.rationale: For example, a function using stop_after_attempt(3) can call itself with an argument that succeeds immediately, then raise on each outer attempt. Every inner call clears and resets the dictionary shared with the active outer call, so the final outer statistics report attempt_number=1 despite three outer attempts. Previously, each invocation's retry controller had its own statistics dictionary. Concurrent async calls likewise corrupt each other's reported statistics.
